title: Status glossary
intro: Every label you see in this module, what it means and what you can do about it.

wt-clean.todo: Nothing to do. This worktree is safe to switch away from or remove.
wt-clean.example: The Changes column shows "No uncommitted changes" once everything is committed.

wt-dirty.todo: Commit or stash the changes before removing the worktree; removing it discards them.
wt-dirty.example: 3 changed files: two edited and one new file.

wt-missing.todo: Run git worktree prune in the repository to forget it.
wt-missing.example: You deleted the folder by hand instead of using git worktree remove.

wt-main.todo: Nothing: it is the repository itself. Remove extra worktrees instead.
wt-main.example: The folder where you cloned the repository.

wt-detached.todo: Create or switch to a branch (git switch -c name) before committing more.
wt-detached.example: You checked out a tag or a commit hash.

wt-sync-none.todo: Push the branch (git push -u origin <branch>) when you want to publish it.
wt-sync-none.example: A new local branch that was never pushed.

wt-sync-synced.example: Shown as a check mark in the table.

wt-sync-ahead.example: Up arrow 2: two local commits are not on the remote yet.

wt-sync-behind.todo: Pull (or fetch and merge) to get them.
wt-sync-behind.example: Down arrow 2: a teammate pushed two commits to the branch.

wt-sync-diverged.todo: Pull or rebase first, then push.
wt-sync-diverged.example: Up 1, down 2: you committed locally while the remote also moved on.

rc-stale.todo: Review it; remove the worktree if the work is finished.
rc-stale.example: A feature branch you stopped working on a month ago.

rc-merged.todo: Safe to remove: the work is already in the base branch.
rc-merged.example: A pull request that was merged last week.

rc-clean.todo: Nothing would be lost by removing it.
rc-clean.example: A worktree where you committed everything.

rc-live.todo: Terminate those processes in the Processes tab first: removal is refused while they run.
rc-live.example: A dev server still running in an old worktree.

rc-orphan.todo: Terminate it: it keeps memory for a folder that is gone.
rc-orphan.example: A node process left over from a worktree you deleted.

rc-regenerable.todo: Delete them to free disk; the tool recreates them when needed.
rc-regenerable.example: node_modules or target folders, and the npm or pnpm caches.

pt-unknown.todo: Run DevDeck as administrator to see its folder, or identify it by PID.
pt-unknown.example: A system or elevated service listening on a port.

pt-noproject.todo: Nothing: it is not part of your known projects. Check its folder before terminating.
pt-noproject.example: A database server started from another folder.
